text:
olivia: Heads-up — launching H200 Reserved pools + Burst (preemptible) pools in ca-central-1 and ap-south-1 next month. This is a controlled rollout: reserved pools for committed customers and a separate burst pool for short-term capacity at higher unit pricing. Docs + migration guide are linked below.

suhas: Nice — any change to SLA or preemption windows for burst?

olivia: Good q. Reserved pools keep existing SLA. Burst pools are preemptible (30–120s notice) and have NO uptime SLA — intended for asynchronous batch workloads or best-effort inference. We'll publish preemption probability curves per zone.

maria: Billing impact? Are customers charged differently if a request falls back from burst to reserved?

olivia: Billing: burst = higher per-token rate + 1-minute minimum charge for a session. If we transparently fall back to reserved, we bill at the rate of the final serving pool. We'll annotate invoices with pool_id tags so customers can filter.

kevin: API changes for customers who want to opt into burst vs reserved?

olivia: Two small params in the provisioning API and CLI: `reserved_capacity_type: "reserved" | "burst"` and `max_preemptible_latency_ms` (optional). Example: 

```
redwoodctl reservations create --model h200 --region ca-central-1 --capacity 8 --type reserved
redwoodctl reservations create --model h200 --region ap-south-1 --capacity 16 --type burst --max-preemptible-latency-ms 2000
```

ezra: From SRE side: need to ensure autoscaler treats burst pools as single-use, avoid moving stateful KV caches to them. Also we should lock down fallback rules so traffic doesn't thrash between pools.

olivia: Agreed. Autoscaler policy will treat burst as "ephemeral" and won't warm KV caches there. Fallback policy is prioritized: reserved -> dedicated-compat -> burst (i.e., only route to burst if explicitly requested or no reserved available and customer opted in). We'll add config flags to override but defaults are conservative.

ops-bot: [capacity-report] ca-central-1: predicted H200 reserved capacity available: 72 GPUs; burst pool cap: 24. ap-south-1: predicted reserved: 56; burst: 40.

maria: Will we auto-migrate existing L4/RTX reservations to H200 for eligible customers?

olivia: No automatic migrations. We'll open an opt-in migration window for eligible customers (60 days). Customers on committed contracts will get a migration credit calculator in the console and a one-click migration for identical instance counts.

suhas: Timeline?

olivia: Rollout schedule:
- 2026-05-10: announcement (this thread) & internal docs live
- 2026-05-20: soft preview for a handful of partner customers (invite-only)
- 2026-06-01: GA for Reserved pools in ca-central-1 and ap-south-1
- 2026-06-15: Burst pools enabled cluster-wide in those regions

kevin: Who owns support runbook for preemption incidents?

olivia: SRE + Support co-owned. I'll post the runbook in #eng-sre and tag you, ezra.

ezra: ack — will add escalation steps and playbook for customer-facing comms.

olivia: Links: internal doc: https://redwood.internal/docs/dedicated/h200-capacity-guide (private) · migration wizard (console) · billing FAQ (internal). If you want early access for a customer, DM me with account id and target region.

maria: Thanks — please add a short blurb for AE enablement so sales can position burst correctly.

olivia: On it. Posting AE blurb and slide deck by EOD tomorrow. :rocket: 

suhas: Thanks olivia, looks good.

olivia: Thanks all — ping me for anything else.
